---
title: "Get started"
description: "Install frpp, define a residual law and simulate a first model."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(frpp)
```

## Installation

Install the development package from GitHub:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ksublee/frpp", build_vignettes = FALSE)
```

The default backend requires emhawkes 1.0.0 or later. The optional `state`
backend uses the public shared-kernel API in GitHub development emhawkes
1.0.1.9000. Install that development version when using state calculations:

```{r install-state-backend, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("ksublee/emhawkes", build_vignettes = FALSE)
```

The default bridge works without that API. State requests report an explicit
error when the API is absent. See the
[shared-kernel contract](https://ksublee.github.io/emhawkes/articles/shared-kernel.html).

## Define a model

A model combines an emhawkes kernel with a residual law. The following law has
Gamma shape 2 and rate 2, hence mean 1:

```{r model}
kernel <- methods::new("hspec", mu = 0.3, alpha = 0.2, beta = 1)
law <- residual_law(c(shape = 2, rate = 2),
  dresidual = stats::dgamma, presidual = stats::pgamma,
  qresidual = stats::qgamma, rresidual = stats::rgamma, name = "Gamma(2,2)")
model <- fspec(kernel, law)
model
```

The kernel supplies the baseline and exponential state dynamics. The residual
law supplies the density, distribution, quantile and random-generation functions.
Constructing these objects does not run the residual callbacks.

For simulation, the current implementation requires equal decay rates within
each row of the kernel matrix. Numeric marked effects and kernel mappings are
supported; more general callbacks use the compatibility backend.


## Supply residual functions as needed

Use the same names as emhawkes: `dresidual` (density), `presidual` (CDF),
`qresidual` (quantile) and `rresidual` (generator). All default to NULL.
The constructor needs at least a density or generator; each operation then
checks only its own requirements before evaluating callbacks or drawing randomness.

| Operation | Required residual functions |
|---|---|
| Simulation | rresidual |
| Univariate likelihood and fitting | dresidual |
| Multivariate likelihood and fitting | dresidual, presidual |
| Residual diagnostics with infer = TRUE | dresidual, presidual, qresidual |

For simulation alone:

```{r residual-generator-only}
simulation_law <- frpp::residual_law(c(rate = 1), rresidual = stats::rexp)
simulation_model <- frpp::fspec(
  methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1), simulation_law)
simulation_path <- frpp::fsim(simulation_model, size = 5, seed = 73,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
simulation_path$inter_arrival
```

The aliases `density`, `cdf`, `quantile` and `rng` remain supported without
warnings, in that order. You can mix names for different roles, but supplying
both non-NULL names for one role is an error. The original six positional
arguments retain their order. Saved laws retain their existing internal
representation and callback environments/defaults; no conversion is needed.

## Simulate and inspect a path

```{r simulation}
path <- fsim(model, size = 1000, seed = 73, lambda_component0 = 0)
head(data.frame(time = cumsum(path$inter_arrival),
  type = path$type, mark = path$mark))
```

`size` includes the initial row, so this request generates 999 events.
`inter_arrival`, `type` and `mark` start with zero. Event types index rows of the
driver, while `type_col_map` selects kernel columns updated after each event.
`N` and `Nc` contain event counts and accumulated marks.

`lambda_component0` contains initial intensity components **excluding the
baseline**. A scalar expands to every component; a matrix must match the kernel
shape. FRPP's automatic rule selects zero, with a message recommending an
explicit state. A Hawkes stationary mean is not assumed for a general residual law.

The standard interface returns the same path:

```{r standard-simulation}
same_path <- stats::simulate(model, size = 1000, seed = 73,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
stopifnot(identical(path, same_path))
```

With an explicit `seed`, the caller's RNG kind and state are restored, including
on errors. With `seed = NULL`, simulation advances the caller's RNG normally.

## Evaluate the likelihood

```{r likelihood}
logLik(model, path$inter_arrival, path$type, mark = path$mark,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
```

Include the initial row when supplying observations. For a univariate model,
`type` may be omitted. Use the same initial components and initial counts used
for the observation window.

With `infer = TRUE`, the result also contains driver states, component histories
and residual diagnostics. These driving quantities are not automatically the
conditional intensities of a general FRPP.

Continue with [Fitting and inference](fitting-and-inference.html), or see
the [multivariate examples](frpp-examples.html).


## Optional independent simulator

The default simulator remains the compatibility bridge. With current GitHub
development emhawkes, choose `fsim(model, backend = "state", ...)` to use the
independent numeric FRPP event loop. It preserves global residual refresh and
path/RNG behavior, but is currently slower on larger paths. Event callbacks
remain in the bridge. `backend = "auto"` opts into capability-based selection;
see [Model and computation](model-and-computation.html) for the support contract.
